objective: Screen for alcohol withdrawal on admission and use the CIWA-Ar scale to judge the need for medically supervised withdrawal management

sources.note: Relayed from the REQ-233 NCLEX-RN cases (read 2026-11-11, primary PDF), not re-read: Psychosocial Integrity includes chemical and other dependencies (withdrawal and toxicity); Reduction of Risk Potential includes recognizing changes in the client's condition.
The objective and secondary objectives are the course's own titles.

sources.cite: American Society of Addiction Medicine. The ASAM Clinical Practice Guideline on Alcohol Withdrawal Management (adopted 2020-01-23)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 in the primary PDF through a summarizing fetch with quotes (the first part of the document): mild withdrawal 'e.g., CIWA-Ar score <10', moderate 'CIWA-Ar scores 10-18', severe at 19 (the comparison sign was lost in the extracted text); symptom-triggered treatment is the preferred benzodiazepine dosing method (V.23); reassess every 1-4 hours for 24 hours as clinically indicated (V.1); thiamine 100 mg IV or IM daily for 3-5 days is typical, and thiamine and glucose may be given in any order (V.7); a history of withdrawal delirium or withdrawal seizure raises the risk of complicated withdrawal (II.5), and when that risk is known treat more aggressively (VII.13); restraints only when required to prevent injury from agitation or violence (VI.12).

sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 through a summarizing fetch with quotes; the page did not show its title or update date: signs may begin within hours of the last drink and peak around 72 hours; withdrawal seizures 'typically occur between 8 and 48 hours'; delirium tremens 3 to 8 days after cessation (the page also says 3 to 5).

sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 through a summarizing fetch: ten items (nausea and vomiting, tremor, anxiety, agitation, paroxysmal sweats, tactile, auditory and visual disturbances, headache, each 0-7; orientation 0-4; 67 at most); PRN medication for a total of 10 or higher under the symptom-triggered method. Used for the items and the trigger; one hospital's form, not a guideline.

brief.situation: 02:00 on a medical unit. You are the RN. Mr. Dale, 54, was admitted at 18:00 with cellulitis of his left leg. The nursing assistant says he is sweaty, shaking, and keeps trying to get out of bed to 'go home and sort things out'.
handover: Admission note: 'drinks socially'; no alcohol screen was done. IV cefazolin running on schedule. Glucose at 22:00 was 118 mg/dL.

Standing alcohol withdrawal protocol (active for every admission): score the CIWA-Ar; lorazepam at the protocol dose IV for a score of 10 or more, then rescore 1 hour after each dose; thiamine 100 mg IV daily; notify the provider for a score of 19 or more, a seizure, hallucinations, or a history of withdrawal seizures or delirium.
No benzodiazepine or thiamine has been given yet.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Scoring the CIWA-Ar and the drug's effect take a few minutes.
Partway through you are asked to write what is happening. The case ends at 04:00, then a debrief scores what you did.

source.note: Untreated, his withdrawal climbs from a CIWA-Ar of about 14 to a seizure in under 2 hours; he has a history of withdrawal delirium. FLAG. Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model.

One protocol dose lowers the score by about 4 points. FLAG. Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model.
About 5 min to effect after an IV dose. FLAG. Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model.
A dose covers him for about 90 min in this case. FLAG. Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model.

A withdrawal seizure at a CIWA-Ar near 27 in this case; seizure timing in the literature is 8 to 48 hours after the last drink (StatPearls), which his 12 hours falls inside. FLAG. Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model.
Tactile hallucinations near a CIWA-Ar of 20. FLAG. Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model.
Three doses within about half an hour oversedate him. FLAG. Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model.

why.question: What is happening to Mr. Dale, how serious is it, and what do you do in what order?

parts.label: Recognition and risk
parts.criteria: Names alcohol withdrawal about 12 hours after the last drink; uses the CIWA-Ar score to grade it (10-18 moderate, 19 or more severe); names the past withdrawal delirium as a risk of complicated withdrawal, with seizures possible in the next day or two.
parts.modelAnswer: Alcohol withdrawal, about 12 hours after his last drink, CIWA-Ar 14: moderate. He had withdrawal delirium two years ago, so he is at high risk of a complicated course; seizures can come in the next 8 to 48 hours.

parts.label: Actions
parts.criteria: Treats by the symptom-triggered protocol: a dose for a score of 10 or more and a rescore an hour later; thiamine; seizure and fall precautions; calls the provider with the score, the last drink and the history; avoids restraints and doses with no score behind them.
parts.modelAnswer: Lorazepam now for the score of 14, rescore in an hour and dose again only if it is 10 or more. Thiamine 100 mg IV. Seizure and fall precautions, a calm lit room, no restraints. SBAR to the provider: score, last drink at 14:00, past delirium.

noProgress.rationale: Withdrawal not brought under the protocol by 04:05 is left to run toward a seizure, so the case calls it harm.

expertPath.text: Ask about drinking: 12 beers a day, last drink 14:00, withdrawal delirium two years ago. Vital signs.
Score the CIWA-Ar: 14, moderate. Seizure and fall precautions while you score.
Lorazepam by the protocol for a score of 10 or more. Thiamine 100 mg IV. SBAR to the provider with the score, the last drink and the history.
Rescore an hour after the dose: under 10, so no further dose. Keep scoring through the night.

seizure.headline: A withdrawal seizure
seizure.body: Moderate withdrawal at 12 hours, with past delirium, needs the protocol now: score, dose for 10 or more, rescore. Untreated or provoked, it climbs to a seizure.

oversedated.headline: Oversedated
oversedated.body: Symptom-triggered dosing means a dose for a score, then a rescore before the next. Stacked doses with no score behind them oversedate.

controlled.headline: Withdrawal controlled by the protocol
controlled.body: You took the history, scored the CIWA-Ar before treating, dosed for the score, rescored an hour later, gave thiamine, kept him safe without restraints and told the provider about his high-risk history. That is the expert path.

controlledLate.headline: No seizure, by a slower or riskier route
controlledLate.body: Check whether you asked about the last drink and past withdrawal, scored before dosing, dosed within 15 minutes of a score of 10 or more, and rescored within the hour.

time_up.headline: Still unresolved
time_up.body: Withdrawal needs a score, a dose for the score, and a rescore.

scoring.modelReasoning: Sweating, tremor and agitation 12 hours after the last drink is alcohol withdrawal, and the admission screen missed it. The CIWA-Ar grades it: under 10 mild, 10 to 18 moderate, 19 or more severe (ASAM 2020). His past withdrawal delirium makes complicated withdrawal more likely, and seizures typically come 8 to 48 hours after the last drink. Treat by symptom-triggered protocol: lorazepam for a score of 10 or more, rescore an hour later, dose again only for a qualifying score. Give thiamine. Keep him safe with seizure and fall precautions in a calm, lit room; restraints are for preventing injury, not for keeping a frightened man in bed, and they worsen agitation. Tell the provider the score, the last drink and the history so the plan can match the risk.

ciwaQ.ask: While you score: under the ASAM 2020 guideline, what CIWA-Ar total marks severe withdrawal?
ciwaQ.explain: ASAM 2020 calls a CIWA-Ar under 10 mild, 10 to 18 moderate and 19 or more severe.
